title: Fluid Rates
desc: Maintenance and dehydration-deficit fluid rates for dogs (60 ml/kg/day) and cats (45 ml/kg/day), with the potassium supplementation table and Mandelker's SQ fluid/furosemide protocol. Clinician reference.

meds.name: Maintenance rate — dog
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'60 ml/kg/day = '+R2(kg*60)+' ml/day = '+R2(kg*60/24)+' ml/hr.
Twice maintenance = '+R2(kg*120/24)+' ml/hr ('+R2(kg*120)+' ml/day).'

meds.name: Deficit by % dehydration — dog
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>{var p=[3,5,7,9,11];return 'Deficit (ml) = % dehydration × kg × 10
'+p.map(function(x){var d=x*kg*10;return x+'% → '+R2(d)+' ml  (over 6 h '+R2(d/6)+', 8 h '+R2(d/8)+', 12 h '+R2(d/12)+', 24 h '+R2(d/24)+' ml/hr)';}).join('
');}
meds.note: Replacement rates are the deficit alone. Day 1 is usually replacement PLUS maintenance; day 2 is maintenance only.

meds.name: Maintenance rate — cat
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'45 ml/kg/day = '+R2(kg*45)+' ml/day = '+R2(kg*45/24)+' ml/hr.
Twice maintenance = '+R2(kg*90/24)+' ml/hr ('+R2(kg*90)+' ml/day).'
meds.note: Cats are 45 ml/kg/day, NOT the canine 60 — this is the number most easily carried across by mistake.

meds.name: Deficit by % dehydration — cat
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>{var p=[3,5,7,9,11];return 'Deficit (ml) = % dehydration × kg × 10
'+p.map(function(x){var d=x*kg*10;return x+'% → '+R2(d)+' ml  (over 6 h '+R2(d/6)+', 8 h '+R2(d/8)+', 12 h '+R2(d/12)+', 24 h '+R2(d/24)+' ml/hr)';}).join('
');}
meds.note: A typical feline plan on the source sheet is twice maintenance plus deficit correction over 12 hours on day 1, dropping to twice maintenance on day 2.

meds.name: SQ fluids with furosemide
meds.doseText: 200 ml lactated Ringer's SQ every 3 to 4 hours (600–900 ml per day), each time WITH 0.2 to 0.3 ml furosemide SQ
meds.note: Hospitalise for 1 to 2 days and treat intensively to lower BUN and creatinine. The furosemide must be given at the SAME TIME as every SQ bolus — it paralyses the sodium/potassium pump, forcing sodium out and taking the SQ fluid with it, flushing the urea toxins out of the body.

notes.Maintenance rates: Dogs 60 ml/kg/day. Cats 45 ml/kg/day. Do not carry the canine figure across to a cat.
notes.Deficit formula: Fluid deficit in ml = % dehydration × body weight in kg × 10.
notes.Day 1 vs day 2: Day 1 is replacement plus maintenance. Day 2 is maintenance only (or twice maintenance in the feline example on the sheet).
notes.Potassium — serum K+ under 2.0: Add 20 mEq KCl per 250 ml, or 80 mEq per litre. MAXIMUM fluid rate 6 ml/kg/hr.
notes.Potassium — serum K+ 2.1 to 2.5: Add 15 mEq per 250 ml, or 60 mEq per litre. Maximum rate 8 ml/kg/hr.
notes.Potassium — serum K+ 2.6 to 3.0: Add 10 mEq per 250 ml, or 40 mEq per litre. Maximum rate 12 ml/kg/hr.
notes.Potassium — serum K+ 3.1 to 3.5: Add 7 mEq per 250 ml, or 28 mEq per litre. Maximum rate 18 ml/kg/hr.
notes.Potassium — serum K+ 3.6 to 5.0: Add 5 mEq per 250 ml, or 20 mEq per litre. Maximum rate 25 ml/kg/hr.
notes.KCl safety: MARK 'DO NOT FLUSH' on any line carrying high-potassium fluid. The maximum infusion rates above exist because a potassium bolus is fatal.
notes.Mandelker SQ protocol: Hospitalise the cat 1–2 days. Lactated Ringer's 200 ml SQ every 3–4 hours, 600–900 ml total per day, and EACH TIME give 0.2–0.3 ml furosemide SQ at the same time.
